prompt.context_jp: 内線が鳴り、鏑木は電話を取った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 話題___またしても、あの新人技師のことらしかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'the topic' as the theme of the sentence.

feedback.correct_en: 話題 is being set up as the theme ('as for the topic...'). は marks it as the frame about which something is said.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 話題 as new information being identified, which doesn't fit — the sentence comments on what the topic was.

contrast_examples.jp: 話題は彼のことだった。

contrast_examples.en: Suddenly the topic changed. (event / new info)

prompt.context_jp: 院内での彼の振る舞いは、医師たちの間で不評をかっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 何しろ人付き合い___苦手な五十嵐は、周囲との調整をほとんど省いてしまう。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside the relative clause 'bad at socializing'.

feedback.correct_en: In the ~が苦手 pattern, が marks the thing one is bad at. Inside a relative clause modifying 五十嵐, が is the natural choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a short relative clause here would sound off and break the modifier structure. 苦手/上手/好き take が for the object of the feeling.

prompt.context_jp: 電話越しに、医師の声はますます棘を含んでいった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鏑木の表情___、みるみるうちに険しくなっていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Kaburaki's expression as the ongoing topic.

feedback.correct_en: The scene is continuing with Kaburaki as established referent; 表情 is being commented on as 'what happened to it' — the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 表情 sound like fresh news being introduced; the narrative has already zoomed in on him.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の表情は暗くなった。

prompt.context_jp: 広瀬は仲間からの視線を浴びて、思わず肩をすくめた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 技師長の姿も、五十嵐の姿___、なぜか見当たらない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the second item in the parallel 'neither X nor Y' listing.

feedback.correct_en: The pattern is '〜も〜も見当たらない' — 'neither one nor the other can be found.' も parallels the first も.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would break the parallel listing. が wouldn't work either because this is additive listing of absent items.

contrast_examples.en: Neither my father nor my mother is home.

contrast_examples.jp: 猫はいるが犬はいない。
contrast_examples.en: There's a cat but no dog. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 整形外科の一角、シャウカステンの前に立っていた五十嵐は、ある小さな影に釘付けになっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: フィルム___写る少年の膝の骨には、成長痛では説明のつかない気配があった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle meaning 'on/in' the film (where the image appears).

feedback.correct_en: 〜に写る means 'appears on/in (a medium).' に marks the surface or medium where something is depicted.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mean 'by means of the film,' which doesn't fit this stative 'image shown on film' meaning. を doesn't work with 写る (intransitive).

contrast_examples.en: A smile appearing in the photo.

prompt.context_jp: 「健太郎君？ 彼ならレントゲンで異常は見られず 成長痛と診断されたんじゃなかったですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「命に関わる病気の可能性___あります 早急な検査が必要なんです」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle presenting a possibility as newly introduced information.

feedback.correct_en: Igarashi is introducing new information to persuade the team: 'there IS a possibility.' With ある, が typically marks newly introduced existents.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply 'as for the possibility (we already discussed), it exists,' but no such possibility was previously established.

prompt.context_jp: 医師のオーダーを待たずに検査に踏み込むことは、医療倫理の際どい線を歩む行為でもある。
prompt.prompt_jp: それでも彼の頭にあったの___、少年とその母親のことだけだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle used in a cleft-like 'the only thing was X' structure.

feedback.correct_en: The 〜のは〜だった cleft frames 'what was in his head' as the topic, with 'the boy and his mother' as the comment. は marks the clefted theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would read as exhaustive identification but the のは…だ cleft naturally takes は, and swapping it in sounds unnatural in this narration.

prompt.context_jp: 「この膝の白い部分は何ですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「関節液です 関節液___水成分でＴ2強調画像では白く写ります」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle introducing joint fluid's property as an explanation.

feedback.correct_en: Igarashi defines what joint fluid IS. は marks the subject of a general/characterizing statement: 'As for joint fluid, it is a water component...'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present joint fluid as freshly spotted info, but here it's being explained as a concept — classic topic-comment territory.

contrast_examples.en: There was a whale! (sighting / new info)

prompt.context_jp: 小野寺が五十嵐を守るために鏑木と対峙している。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「責任なら 私___取ります」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'I (and no one else) will take responsibility.'

feedback.correct_en: Onodera is exhaustively identifying himself as the one who will bear responsibility — 'It is I who will take it.' が marks exhaustive-listing identification.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weaken it to 'as for me, I'll take it,' losing the dramatic 'I'm the one' assertion the scene demands.

contrast_examples.en: As for me, I'll do it. (contrastive)

prompt.context_jp: 小野寺が鏑木に反論している場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「この検査___1人の少年とその母親の未来がかかってます」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what the future 'hangs on.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜に〜がかかる means 'X depends on/hangs on Y.' に marks the thing that something is riding on.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would read as 'by means of this test,' which misses the 'depends on' idiom. を doesn't fit this intransitive structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 合否は試験にかかっている。

contrast_examples.en: Passed by means of the exam.

prompt.context_jp: 甘春が母親に骨肉腫を説明する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「50万人に1人___なるといわれる 大変 珍しい病気です」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle marking 'one in 500,000' as the subject of 'become ill.'

feedback.correct_en: Inside the relative clause '50万人に1人がなる,' が marks '1 in 500,000' as the subject that develops the disease. Subjects inside relative clauses take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は generally cannot appear as the subject marker inside a relative clause of this type. を doesn't work with the intransitive なる.

contrast_examples.jp: この病気は子供がなる。
contrast_examples.en: This disease — children get it. (main-clause topic)

prompt.context_jp: 黒羽が若手に対して突き放すように語っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「技師の仕事___検査したら それで終わり」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle framing 'the technician's job' as the topic being defined.

feedback.correct_en: She's making a general statement defining 'the technician's job.' は marks it as the thematic subject of a characterizing claim.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like freshly discovered info, but she's stating a role/principle she wants to assert.

contrast_examples.jp: 私の仕事は教えることだ。

prompt.context_jp: 健太郎の母、美佐子が息子を励ます場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「50万人に1人とか そんなの関係ない 健太郎___1分の1 かけがえのない存在なの」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the emphatic topic 'Kentaro' set against the statistics.

feedback.correct_en: She contrasts the earlier '1 in 500,000' with 'as for Kentaro — he is 1 of 1.' は gives the contrastive topic frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark Kentaro as newly identified, but the emotional punch comes from contrasting him against the statistical frame — which は carries.

contrast_examples.jp: 他の人はどうあれ、君は特別だ。
contrast_examples.en: Whatever others may be, you are special. (contrast)
You are the special one. (exhaustive id)

prompt.context_jp: 小野寺が離婚届を手にしながら自嘲する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「夫婦ってのは いいもんですよね 関係___悪化すれば こんな紙切れ1枚でね スパッと 別れられるんですからね」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'the relationship' inside a conditional clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate 〜すれば conditional, the subject typically takes が. 関係が悪化すれば = 'if the relationship worsens.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this short conditional feels out of place; conditionals embed neutral subjects with が. を doesn't work with intransitive 悪化する.

contrast_examples.jp: 天気が悪ければ中止だ。
contrast_examples.en: If the weather is bad, it's canceled.

contrast_examples.jp: 天気は良くないが行く。
contrast_examples.en: The weather isn't good, but I'll go. (contrast topic)

prompt.context_jp: 同僚たちが技師長の家族の噂をしている場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あんなんだから 妻子___出ていかれるんでしょうね」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the agent in this suffering-passive.

feedback.correct_en: In the passive 出ていかれる (adversity passive), the agent who did the leaving is marked with に. 'He was left by his wife and kids.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark them as the subject of 出ていく, but the verb here is passive 出ていかれる — the subject is the one suffering, and the leaver takes に.

contrast_examples.en: He was abandoned by his wife.

prompt.context_jp: 鏑木が小野寺に圧力をかけるセリフ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「秩序を___人間は 一刻も早く追い出した方が この病院のためなんですがね」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb collocating with 秩序 ('order').

feedback.correct_en: 秩序を乱す ('to disturb/disrupt order') is the standard collocation, and 'disruptor of order' is the chapter's title theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: 壊す (break/smash) and 崩す (collapse/break down) are physical/structural; they don't fit the social-order idiom.

prompt.context_jp: 小野寺が鏑木の圧力に耐える場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 去っていく後ろ姿を見送りながら、小野寺は奥歯を___。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb completing the idiom for suppressing anger.

feedback.correct_en: 奥歯を噛みしめる is a set expression for enduring strong emotion like anger or sorrow — biting down to hold it in.
feedback.incorrect_en: 抜く (pull out) and 磨く (polish) are literal dental actions that don't carry the emotional-restraint meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 悔しさに奥歯を噛みしめる。
contrast_examples.en: To bite down one's molars in frustration.

prompt.context_jp: 鏑木が整形外科医からの電話を受けて謝るセリフ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___ はい 今すぐに」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the standard formal apology phrase.

feedback.correct_en: 申し訳ありません is the proper apology to a complaining colleague/doctor in a hospital workplace — formal and contrite.
feedback.incorrect_en: ごめんなさい is casual/childlike and inappropriate here. 失礼しました means 'excuse me (for a minor breach)' and is too weak for an actual complaint.

contrast_examples.jp: 大変申し訳ありません。

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐がフィルムを見つめる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 病変が隠れている可能性は、___——彼の直感はそう告げていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the set phrase meaning 'cannot be ruled out.'

choices.text: あるにこしたことはない

feedback.correct_en: なきにしもあらず is a literary set phrase meaning 'it's not that there isn't (any)' — i.e., the possibility can't be denied.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other phrases mean 'it's best to have' and 'is indispensable,' which don't fit a hedging statement about hidden lesions.

contrast_examples.jp: 可能性はなきにしもあらずだ。
保険はあるにこしたことはない。

prompt.context_jp: 鏑木がVIP患者の金田会長を出迎える場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鏑木は駆けつけ、___頭を下げた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adverb for a deep, apologetic bow.

feedback.correct_en: 深々と頭を下げる is the standard collocation for bowing deeply, often in apology or deep respect — perfect for this scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: 細々と means 'in a small/modest way' and 淡々と means 'matter-of-factly' — neither matches a desperate deep bow.

prompt.context_jp: 鏑木が怒鳴るセリフ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ふざけるな！ 医師のオーダーもなく 勝手なことして 懲戒免職だけじゃ ___ませんよ！」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb completing 'won't end with just...'

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけじゃ済まされない is a fixed expression meaning 'won't be settled with just…' / 'won't end there,' used as a threat.
feedback.incorrect_en: 終わる and 止まる don't form this idiom with 済ます. The passive-potential 済まされる is the fixed form for 'cannot be settled.'

contrast_examples.jp: 謝るだけじゃ済まされない。
contrast_examples.en: Just an apology won't settle it.

prompt.context_jp: T1画像に異常な影が映った瞬間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 浮かび上がった影に、広瀬は思わず息を___。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for 'to catch one's breath' in shock.

feedback.correct_en: 息を呑む is the fixed idiom for being so startled or awestruck that one swallows one's breath — perfect for seeing an alarming medical image.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息を吐く means 'exhale' (often relief) and 息を吸う is just 'inhale' — neither captures sudden shock.

contrast_examples.jp: あまりの美しさに息を呑んだ。
contrast_examples.en: Caught my breath at the beauty.
Let out a sigh of relief.

prompt.context_jp: 甘春が小野寺に感謝するセリフ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「おかげで 健太郎君の病気に ___ことができました」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'to notice/discover.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜に気付く means 'to notice/become aware of X.' That's exactly what the team did regarding Kentaro's illness.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気を付ける means 'to be careful,' and 気になる means 'to be bothered/curious about' — neither matches the medical discovery.

prompt.context_jp: 鏑木が小野寺にVIP患者の対応を頼む場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as a boss's polite-but-firm business request?

choices.text: ＶＩＰ患者の方ですから くれぐれも 失礼のないように お願いしますよ
ＶＩＰ患者だから 絶対に 失礼するなよ

feedback.correct_en: The chapter's line uses くれぐれも + 失礼のないように + お願いします — polished business Japanese appropriate for a department head addressing a chief technician.
feedback.incorrect_en: Version B uses blunt casual commands (絶対に…するなよ) that don't fit the smooth, pressure-with-politeness tone Kaburaki uses to subordinates.

contrast_examples.jp: くれぐれもよろしくお願いします。

prompt.context_jp: 甘春が母親に寄り添って励ます場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural as a doctor's warm, supportive closing to a patient's family?

choices.text: どうか 我々を信じてください 一緒に頑張りましょう
我々を信じて どうか 頑張ってください 一緒に

feedback.correct_en: A follows standard rhetorical flow: どうか + request, then a unifying 一緒に頑張りましょう. It sounds like a natural doctor's reassurance.
feedback.incorrect_en: B scrambles どうか and tags 一緒に onto the end as an afterthought, which sounds disjointed and unnatural.

contrast_examples.jp: 一緒に頑張りましょう。
どうか信じてください。

prompt.context_jp: 甘春が健太郎に優しく語りかけるベッドサイドの場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for a doctor gently apologizing to a child?

choices.text: ごめんね 大丈夫だなんて 間違ったこと 言っちゃったね
申し訳ございません 大丈夫などと 誤ったことを 申し上げました

feedback.correct_en: Speaking to an 8-year-old patient, soft casual-polite with ごめんね and 言っちゃった matches the warm bedside register.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses stiff humble business keigo (申し訳ございません / 申し上げました) that is wildly out of place when comforting a child.

contrast_examples.en: Sorry, I said too much. (warm casual)

contrast_examples.jp: 申し訳ございませんでした。

prompt.context_jp: 大森院長が甘春に五十嵐のことを語るセリフ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural as a mentor's advice?

choices.text: 困った時は彼を頼るといいわ 必ず あなたの力になってくれる
困った時は彼に頼れ 必ず 力になる

feedback.correct_en: A uses 〜といいわ advice and 〜てくれる benefactive, which naturally conveys a senior woman's warm recommendation about someone else.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is a blunt imperative without benefactive — it sounds like a drill-sergeant order, not a mentor describing a trustworthy colleague.
